### TaskForge Update: Report Export (Task 10) #### 1. Goal Enhance TaskForge CLI to export gate summaries (including overviews, recent tasks, and invariants) as Markdown and HTML files, enabling easy publication or sharing in the RazorCascade reliability study. Build on existing JSON summary generation for seamless integration. #### 2. Proposed Implementation Details - Add a new `export` subcommand via commander.js: `taskforge export --format [md|html] --output [path]`. - Extend `generateSummary()` to optionally trigger export after JSON write. - Introduce `generateMarkdown(summary: Summary)` and `generateHTML(summary: Summary)` functions: - Markdown: Use template literals for structured output (e.g., `# Task Overview\n- Total: ${overview.total}\n## Invariants\n${invariants.join('\n')}`). - HTML: Generate simple semantic markup (e.g., `

Task Overview

  • Total: ${overview.total}
`) with basic CSS for readability. - Read from `~/.taskforge/summary.json`, transform, and write atomically to user-specified output (default: `./taskforge-report.[md|html]`). - Leverage Bun's `Bun.write()` for efficient file ops; no external deps needed. #### 3. Validation or Testing - Unit tests with Bun's test runner: Mock summary JSON, assert exported files match expected Markdown/HTML strings (e.g., test edge cases like empty tasks or high tag frequencies). - Integration test: Run CLI end-to-end in a temp dir, verify file contents and atomicity (no partial writes). - Manual validation: Generate reports from sample datasets and check rendering in browsers/Markdown viewers. #### 4. Risks - Formatting inconsistencies across renderers (e.g., Markdown flavors or HTML escaping issues) could lead to unreadable outputs. - Large task histories may increase export time/memory usage, exacerbating existing history overhead. - User-specified paths risk overwriting files; mitigate with confirmation prompts or safe defaults.
